section: Indus Valley Civilization - discovery, chronology, geographical extent, boundary sites
subsections: Site → river and present state/district - Indian vs Pakistani sites

accepted.s: Mohenjodaro is located in which of the following present-day regions?
accepted.x: Mohenjodaro lies in Sindh province of Pakistan, near Larkana, on the Indus River.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the present-day locations of major Pakistani Harappan cities.
accepted.sec: Site → river and present state/district - Indian vs Pakistani sites

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Chanhudaro is situated on the Indus in Sindh, Pakistan, near Mohenjodaro.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure site–river pair and verify the present location.
accepted.sec: Site → river and present state/district - Indian vs Pakistani sites

accepted.s: Lothal is situated at the confluence of which rivers?
accepted.x: Lothal lies at the Bhogava–Sabarmati confluence in Ahmedabad district of Gujarat, near the head of the Gulf of Cambay.
accepted.tq: Test the distinctive river association of a site rather than its general state location.
accepted.sec: Site → river and present state/district - Indian vs Pakistani sites

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
a. Kalibangan — Ghaggar — Hanumangarh
b. Ropar — Sutlej — Punjab
c. Alamgirpur — Hindon — Meerut
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All three pairs are correct. Kalibangan is in Hanumangarh, Rajasthan; Ropar is on the Sutlej in Punjab; and Alamgirpur is on the Hindon in Meerut, Uttar Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Check each site against both its river and present district before choosing the code.
accepted.sec: Site → river and present state/district - Indian vs Pakistani sites

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Padri is in Gujarat, but it is not associated here with the Narmada; its river is not specified in the table. Manda is on the Chenab and Daimabad on the Pravara.
accepted.tq: Find the pair containing an unsupported or altered river association.
accepted.sec: Site → river and present state/district - Indian vs Pakistani sites

accepted.s: Which of the following sites is situated in Jammu and Kashmir?
accepted.x: Manda is located on the Chenab in Jammu and Kashmir. Daimabad is in Maharashtra, Padri in Gujarat and Banawali in Haryana.
accepted.tq: Use state-based elimination among geographically distinct Harappan sites.
accepted.sec: Site → river and present state/district - Indian vs Pakistani sites

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Site)
A. Rakhigarhi
B. Banawali
C. Mandi
D. Dholavira
List-II (Present location)
1. Kutch, Gujarat
2. Hisar district, Haryana
3. Muzaffarnagar, Uttar Pradesh
4. Hisar–Fatehabad region, Haryana
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: Rakhigarhi is in Hisar district, Banawali in the Hisar–Fatehabad region, Mandi in Muzaffarnagar and Dholavira in Kutch.
accepted.tq: Start with the distinctive Kutch and Muzaffarnagar locations, then resolve the Haryana pair.
accepted.sec: Site → river and present state/district - Indian vs Pakistani sites

accepted.s: Which one of the following States and site combinations is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Rakhigarhi is in Haryana, not Rajasthan. Kalibangan is the site listed for Rajasthan.
accepted.tq: Use the state-wise concentration table and identify the swapped site.
accepted.sec: Site → river and present state/district - Indian vs Pakistani sites

accepted.s: The highest concentration of Harappan settlements was found in which geographical system?
accepted.x: The Ghaggar–Hakra system had the highest concentration of settlements, with about 250 sites, of which six were cities.
accepted.tq: Associate the quantitative settlement concentration with the correct river system.
accepted.sec: Site → river and present state/district - Indian vs Pakistani sites

accepted.s: Who excavated Harappa in 1921 under the direction of John Marshall?
accepted.x: Daya Ram Sahni excavated Harappa in 1921 under John Marshall. Harappa is regarded as the first site in the discovery sequence.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the excavator of Harappa from those associated with Mohenjodaro and Chanhudaro.

accepted.s: Mohenjodaro was first excavated in 1922 by whom?
accepted.x: R. D. Banerji excavated Mohenjodaro in 1922; later work was associated with Mackay, K. N. Dikshit and Marshall.
accepted.tq: Apply the site–excavator–year association and avoid swapping it with Harappa.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Site)
A. Chanhudaro
B. Ropar
C. Surkotada
D. Banawali
List-II (Excavator)
1. R. S. Bisht
2. J. P. Joshi
3. N. G. Majumdar
4. Y. D. Sharma
Select the correct answer using the code below.
accepted.x: N. G. Majumdar excavated Chanhudaro, Y. D. Sharma Ropar, J. P. Joshi Surkotada and R. S. Bisht Banawali.
accepted.tq: Begin with the less-confusable excavator–site pairs and eliminate crossed combinations.

accepted.s: The excavation of Kalibangan during 1961–69 was associated with which of the following archaeologists?
o: Amarendra Nath, followed by N. G. Majumdar
Ghosh, followed by B. B. Lal and B. K. Thapar
J. P. Joshi, followed by R. S. Bisht
S. R. Rao, followed by Daya Ram Sahni
accepted.x: A. Ghosh began work at Kalibangan in 1953, while B. B. Lal and B. K. Thapar were associated with the excavations of 1961–69.
accepted.tq: Test a multi-stage excavation attribution rather than a single excavator.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Dholavira — J. P. Joshi found it; R. S. Bisht led its excavation
Dholavira — S. R. Rao found it; A. Ghosh led its excavation
Dholavira — Amarendra Nath found it; Y. D. Sharma led its excavation
Dholavira — N. G. Majumdar found it; R. D. Banerji led its excavation
accepted.x: Dholavira was found by J. P. Joshi in 1967–68, and its excavation was led by R. S. Bisht, particularly from 1990 onward.
accepted.tq: Separate discovery from later excavation leadership to avoid the swapped-person trap.

accepted.s: Rakhigarhi was excavated by which archaeologist in 1997?
accepted.x: Amarendra Nath excavated Rakhigarhi in 1997. R. S. Bisht is associated with Banawali and Dholavira excavations.
accepted.tq: Use the year as a confirmation clue for the archaeologist–site pair.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. J. Fleet published Harappan seals
B. Harappan bricks were used as railway ballast
C. Daya Ram Sahni found Harappa
D. Charles Masson described the ruins of Harappa
accepted.x: Charles Masson described the ruins during 1826–38, railway ballast use occurred in 1857, J. Fleet published seals in 1912 and Sahni found Harappa in 1921–22.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest events first, then place the 1857 and 1912 developments between them.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about the discovery timeline is correct?
o: Wheeler excavated Mohenjodaro in 1922 immediately after its discovery.
J. Fleet published Harappan seals in 1912, before Sahni’s discovery of Harappa.
Charles Masson described Harappa’s ruins only after the railway excavations of 1857.
Sahni discovered Harappa in 1950 after Wheeler’s excavation.
accepted.x: J. Fleet published Harappan seals in 1912, while Daya Ram Sahni found Harappa in 1921–22. Wheeler’s work at Mohenjodaro belongs to 1950.
accepted.tq: Use chronological contradiction to reject statements that reverse the discovery sequence.

accepted.s: Which of the following sites is regarded as the westernmost Harappan port on the Makran coast?
accepted.x: Sutkagendor was a Harappan westernmost coastal town or port on the Makran coast.
accepted.tq: Match the superlative geographical description with the appropriate boundary site.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the easternmost Harappan site?
accepted.x: Alamgirpur, a Late Harappan site in Meerut district of Uttar Pradesh, is identified as the easternmost Harappan site.
accepted.tq: Distinguish eastern and western boundary sites by their geographical descriptions.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Kot Diji was a pre-Harappan fortified settlement in Sindh.
2. Kot Diji was destroyed by fire.
3. Kot Diji is situated in Gujarat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Kot Diji was a pre-Harappan fortified settlement in Sindh and was destroyed by fire. Statement 3 is false because Kot Diji is in Sindh, Pakistan.
accepted.tq: Check the two descriptive facts separately from the deliberately shifted location.

accepted.s: Surkotada is particularly associated with which archaeological finding?
o: Horse bones, though the identification is disputed
The earliest known gold coin hoard
accepted.x: Surkotada is a fortified Harappan site in Kutch associated with horse bones; the interpretation is disputed.
accepted.tq: Identify the distinctive but qualified finding and retain the caution in the wording.

accepted.s: Rakhigarhi is notable because it is regarded as which of the following?
o: The largest Harappan site in India
accepted.x: Rakhigarhi is identified as the largest Harappan site in India and is located in Haryana.
accepted.tq: Match the site with its size-based distinction rather than its river basin alone.

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
A. Sutkagendor — Harappan westernmost coastal town
B. Sohgaura — Mauryan copper-plate site
C. Pataliputra — Harappan city
D. Mehrgarh — Neolithic site
accepted.x: A, B and D are correct. Pataliputra was a later Magadhan and Mauryan capital, not a Harappan city.
accepted.tq: Spot the wrong civilizational classification and select the combination of correct pairs.

accepted.s: Mehrgarh is classified in relation to the Harappan sites as which of the following?
o: A Neolithic site dating to about 7000 BCE
A Harappan port on the Makran coast
A Late Harappan site in Uttar Pradesh
accepted.x: Mehrgarh is a Neolithic site dating to approximately 7000 BCE; it is not classified as a Harappan site in the listed comparison.
accepted.tq: Use the civilizational-period distinction to separate Mehrgarh from Harappan sites.

accepted.s:
Which of the following sites are located in present-day Pakistan?
1. Harappa
2. Mohenjodaro
3. Chanhudaro
4. Lothal
accepted.x: Harappa, Mohenjodaro and Chanhudaro are in Pakistan. Lothal is located in Gujarat, India.
accepted.tq: Classify each site by present national boundary, not by its ancient cultural association.
accepted.sec: Site → river and present state/district - Indian vs Pakistani sites

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the Harappan sites listed in Uttar Pradesh?
o: Rakhigarhi and Banawali are located in Uttar Pradesh.
Dholavira and Surkotada are located in Uttar Pradesh.
Kalibangan and Alamgirpur are both located in Uttar Pradesh.
Mandi and Hulas are located in Uttar Pradesh.
accepted.x: Mandi is in Muzaffarnagar and Hulas in Saharanpur, both in Uttar Pradesh. Rakhigarhi and Banawali are in Haryana, while Dholavira and Surkotada are in Gujarat.
accepted.tq: Use paired regional identification and eliminate sites belonging to Haryana, Gujarat and Rajasthan.
accepted.sec: Site → river and present state/district - Indian vs Pakistani sites
